newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Millennium bug to cost Kredietbank as much as Euro.
newsitem.headline: Millennium bug to cost Kredietbank as much as Euro.

text.p: Belgian Kredietbank said on Thursday that adapting its computer networks to the switch into the new century will cost it nearly one billion francs, as much as preparing for Europe's single currency.

"The cost of switching our systems to the year 2000 will be comparable to that of what the switch to the Euro will cost us -- just under one billion francs," Kredietbank executive committee member Herman Agneessens said at a news conference about first-half 1996 earnings.

Many companies have worried that the year 2000 will cause havoc in their computer systems, which were never programmed to cope with four digit dates. But few have so far put a figure on the cost of this so-called "Millennium Bug."
"We want to make sure the transfer is smooth. Therefore we are testing all our systems," Agneessens said.
Kredietbank said group net profit rose 14.5 percent to 6.69 billion francs in the six-months to June 30 and that full year profit would be "very good."
